raw_response:
My land is about 6 mu here in Quzhou. My family has farmed it for generations. Winter wheat then summer corn — that's what everyone around here does, that's what the soil knows, and that's what the grain buyer at the village station will purchase. I don't have money to experiment with vegetables or cotton, and I don't have the knowledge for it either. My husband's brother tried cotton years ago and lost money. I won't do that.

For wheat, I'll till the ground with the rotary machine after the corn comes off in September, then sow in mid-October. The seed shop sells the improved variety everyone uses now — I stopped saving my own seed maybe ten years ago because the yields were getting worse. I'll put fertilizer down at sowing and again when the plants start jointing in spring. I pump irrigation water from our well — three times is usually enough: before winter sets in, at jointing, and at heading. I spray twice, once for aphids in spring, once if I see disease. That's what my neighbor does and her wheat looks good.

For corn, I sow right after the wheat harvest in June. No need to plow much — just push the seed in and go. I use the hybrid seed, Zhengdan or whatever the shop has, because it gives more cobs. One irrigation if July is dry. Maybe one spray. Corn mostly takes care of itself here in summer.

I don't grow anything else. Six mu is enough work for me alone while my husband does day labor in Handan city.
